identity.title: Copper-based nanoparticles in antimicrobial and anti-biofilm strategies against gram-negative bacteria: mechanisms, nanocarrier functions, and emerging integrations with advanced biotechnologies.

content.abstract: AIMS: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella pneumoniae is an emerging threat to human health. These pathogens can infect immunosuppressed individuals and cause persistent infections through diverse resistance mechanisms and adaptive strategies, including biofilm formation. This review focuses on the antibacterial and antibiofilm properties of copper-based nanoparticles, with a special emphasis on the underlying mechanisms of antimicrobial action and potential applications in novel antimicrobial strategies. METHODS: Relevant literature published between 2000 and 2026 was identified through searches in PubMed. The search covered copper-based nanostructures, their antibacterial and antibiofilm activities, mechanisms of action, and emerging biotechnological applications, including nanocarrier systems, CRISPR/Cas technologies, and bacteriophage-based strategies. RESULTS: Copper-based nanostructures exhibit antibacterial activity through complementary mechanisms that may involve nanoparticle-cell interactions, copper-ion release, ROS generation, membrane disruption, metalloprotein mismetallation, and damage to intracellular components. Their nanoscale characteristics, particularly high surface area and enhanced copper ion release, further facilitate interactions with bacterial cellular components. Copper-based nanostructures also affect biofilm-associated processes, with some studies reporting changes in quorum-sensing-related gene expression and biofilm development. Moreover, their membrane-permeabilizing properties, ion release and potential for surface functionalization support their investigation as nanocarrier platforms and complementary components of antibiotic, CRISPR/Cas and bacteriophage-based strategies. CONCLUSION: Copper-based nanostructures show potential against resistant Gram-negative pathogens through their diverse antibacterial and antibiofilm activities. Their combination with CRISPR/Cas and bacteriophage-based approaches may further broaden their antimicrobial applications, although further research is needed to establish their effectiveness.
